nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an array with entries in a type $\alpha$, let $k \in \alpha$, let $\mathrm{lt}$ be any Boolean-valued comparison on $\alpha$, and let $\ell$ and $h$ be natural numbers. Lean core's Boolean binary search membership test for $k$ in $A$, with comparison $\mathrm{lt}$ and bounds $\ell$ and $h$, returns true exactly when Lean core's array binary search with the same arguments returns some element.
nodes.title: Array binary search membership test agrees with binary search

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an array with entries in a linearly ordered type, sorted so that an earlier entry is never greater than a later one, and let $k$ be an element of that type. Lean core's Boolean binary search membership test for $k$ over the whole of $A$, with the strict order $<$ as comparison, returns true if and only if $k$ is an entry of $A$.
nodes.title: Binary search membership test on a sorted array is correct

nodes.summary: Let $A = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ be an array of length $n$ with entries in a linearly ordered type, with $a_i \le a_j$ whenever $i < j$. Let $k$ be an element of that type and $\ell$, $h$ natural numbers. Lean core's Boolean binary search membership test for $k$ in $A$, with the strict order $<$ as comparison and inclusive bounds $\ell$ and $h$, returns true if and only if there is an index $i < n$ with…
nodes.title: Bounded binary search membership test on a sorted array is correct

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an array with entries in a linearly ordered type, sorted so that an earlier entry is never greater than a later one, and let $k$ be an element of that type. Lean core's array binary search for $k$ over the whole of $A$, with the strict order $<$ as comparison, returns no element if and only if $k$ is not an entry of $A$.
nodes.title: Binary search on a sorted array fails exactly on non-members

nodes.summary: Let $A = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ be an array of length $n$ with entries in a linearly ordered type, with $a_i \le a_j$ whenever $i < j$. Let $k$ be an element of that type and $\ell$, $h$ natural numbers. Lean core's array binary search for $k$ in $A$, with the strict order $<$ as comparison and inclusive bounds $\ell$ and $h$, returns no element if and only if there is no index $i < n$ with $\ell \le i \le h$ and…
nodes.title: Bounded binary search on a sorted array fails exactly when the key is absent

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an array with entries in a linearly ordered type, sorted so that an earlier entry is never greater than a later one, and let $k$ and $a$ be elements of that type. Lean core's array binary search for $k$ over the whole of $A$, with the strict order $<$ as comparison, returns $a$ if and only if $a = k$ and $k$ is an entry of $A$.
nodes.title: Binary search on a sorted array finds exactly its members

nodes.summary: Let $A = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ be an array of length $n$ with entries in a linearly ordered type, with $a_i \le a_j$ whenever $i < j$. Let $k$ and $a$ be elements of that type and $\ell$, $h$ natural numbers. Lean core's array binary search for $k$ in $A$, with the strict order $<$ as comparison and inclusive bounds $\ell$ and $h$, returns $a$ if and only if $a = k$ and there is an index $i < n$ with…
nodes.title: Result of bounded binary search on a sorted array

nodes.summary: Let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ be an array over a linearly ordered type, sorted in nondecreasing order, and let $k$ be a key. Binary search for the first occurrence of $k$ in $a$ returns no index if and only if $a_i \ne k$ for every $i < n$.
nodes.title: Binary search reports absence exactly when the key is absent

nodes.summary: Let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ be an array over a linearly ordered type, sorted in nondecreasing order, let $k$ be a key and let $i$ be a natural number. Binary search for the first occurrence of $k$ in $a$ returns the index $i$ if and only if $i < n$, $a_i = k$, and $a_j < k$ for every $j < i$.
nodes.title: Binary search returns the first occurrence of the key

nodes.summary: For every array $a$ of length $n$ over a linearly ordered type and every key $k$, binary search for the first occurrence of $k$ in $a$ makes at most $\lceil \log_2 (n + 1) \rceil + 1$ element comparisons.
nodes.title: Comparison bound for binary search for the first occurrence

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be an array of length $n$ over a linearly ordered type, let $k$ be a key, and let $\ell$ be the index returned by lower-bound search for $k$ in $a$. The number of element comparisons made by binary search for the first occurrence of $k$ in $a$ equals the number made by lower-bound search for $k$ in $a$, plus $1$ if $\ell < n$ and plus $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Exact comparison count of binary search for the first occurrence

nodes.summary: Given an array $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ over a linearly ordered type and a key $k$, binary search for the first occurrence of $k$ in $a$ runs lower-bound search for $k$ in $a$, obtaining an index $\ell$. If $\ell < n$, it makes one further comparison, charged one unit, and returns $\ell$ when $a_\ell = k$ and no index otherwise; if $\ell \ge n$, it returns no index without further cost.
nodes.title: Binary search for the first occurrence

nodes.summary: Let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ be an array over a linearly ordered type, sorted in nondecreasing order, let $k$ be a key, and let $\ell$ be the index returned by lower-bound search for $k$ in $a$. Then $\ell \le n$, $a_j < k$ for every $j < \ell$, and $k \le a_j$ for every $j$ with $\ell \le j < n$.
nodes.title: Correctness of lower-bound search

nodes.summary: For every array $a$ of length $n$ over a linearly ordered type and every key $k$, lower-bound search for $k$ in $a$ makes at most $\lceil \log_2 (n + 1) \rceil$ element comparisons.
nodes.title: Comparison bound for lower-bound search

nodes.summary: Given an array $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ over a linearly ordered type and a key $k$, lower-bound search maintains a half-open interval $[l, h)$ of indices, starting from $[0, n)$. While $l < h$, it compares $a_m$ with $k$ at the midpoint $m = l + \lfloor (h - l)/2 \rfloor$, charging one unit for this comparison, and continues with $[m + 1, h)$ if $a_m < k$ and with $[l, m)$ otherwise. When $l = h$ it returns $l$.
nodes.title: Lower-bound search

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
